**Verdict:** Cannot determine from available records

**Confidence:** low, because a search of digital databases did not identify a renewal, but a manual check of the physical Library of Congress records is required to definitively rule out a renewal.

### Evidence
- *The Price of Salt* was first published in 1952 [OL:OL59448W].
- Author Patricia Highsmith (who wrote under the pseudonym Claire Morgan) was born on January 19, 1921, and died on February 4, 1995 [OL:AUTHOR:OL28577A].
- The work was registered for U.S. copyright on April 15, 1952, under registration number A68131, listing the title "The price of salt" by Patricia Highsmith (Claire Morgan) [REG:795B643A-6E97-1014-9357-E9A0C844EAF1].
- No matching renewal registration for original registration A68131, the title *The Price of Salt*, the alternative title *Carol*, or the author names was found in the digital renewal database for the relevant 1979–1981 window [RULE:1952-us-False].

### What these records can't tell us
- Whether a renewal was filed under an alternate title or variant spelling that was not properly linked or indexed in this digital database. A manual search of physical Library of Congress records is necessary to confirm non-renewal.
- Whether the first edition of the book contained a legally valid copyright notice.

### Digitized copies and access
- **Open Library:** A record exists with borrowable ebook access [OL:OL59448W].
- **HathiTrust:** No matching copy was found in the HathiTrust catalog in searches using LCCN 52-8026 and OCLC numbers 32734256 or 22860658.
- **Project Gutenberg:** No matching copy was found in Project Gutenberg in this search.

_Not legal advice. Records: NYPL Catalog of Copyright Entries transcriptions._

### Sources
- `OL:OL59448W` Open Library — https://openlibrary.org/works/OL59448W
- `OL:AUTHOR:OL28577A` Open Library Authors API — https://openlibrary.org/authors/OL28577A
- `REG:795B643A-6E97-1014-9357-E9A0C844EAF1` NYPL Catalog of Copyright Entries — registrations (github.com/NYPL/catalog_of_copyright_entries_project)
- `RULE:1952-us-False` U.S. Copyright Office Circular 15A (Duration) and Circular 22 (How to Investigate the Copyright Status of a Work), https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ22.pdf
